newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50-$1 lower - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50-$1 lower - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by outlooks for continued weak pork product prices, livestock dealers said.

Declines also were expected from hefty hog marketings on Tuesday, which gave packers plenty of hogs for Wednesday operations, they said. The heavy marketings could continue Wednesday, furthering declines, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog receipts Tuesday were estimated at 110,000 head, USDA reported. Actual receipts on Monday were only 90,000 head.

Fresh retail pork cuts at midday were quoted $2.00 to $5.00 per cwt lower for hams, $4.00 lower for pork bellies and $3.00 to $8.00 lower for lean trimmings, according to USDA's central U.S. carlot pork report.
There were 20.5 loads of pork and 10.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen at $60.50 to $61.00. Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range $60.00 to $60.50.
Indiana/Ohio top plant prices for hogs were seen at $60.00, several livestock dealers said.
